pass_a_gloss: Not of old only did Nebuchadnezzar stand up the golden image, nor then only did he threaten Ananias and Azarias and Misael, if they would not bow down, to throw them into the furnace of the fire; but even now Nebuchadnezzar says the same things to us, the crossing-over and genuine Hebrews. But we, in order that we may have trial of heavenly dew quenching every fire away from us and cooling down our leading part, let us imitate those sacred men; perhaps even now Haman wants you, the Mordecais, to bow down to him; but you say: I will not place glory of humans above glory of God, Israel. Let us turn Bel upside down by the word of God and kill the dragon with Daniel, in order that, drawing near to mouths of lions, we may be able to suffer nothing from them, only those responsible to us for the present contest going to be eaten up by the lions not able to gulp us down. Let us hold on to the fact that in the manly deeds of Job this too has been said: having put my hand upon my mouth I kissed, and this then may be reckoned to me the greatest lawlessness; and it is likely that they will command us to put the hand to the mouth and kiss.
pass_b_english: It was not only long ago that Nebuchadnezzar set up the “golden image” (Daniel 3:1), nor only then that he threatened Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael that, if they did not worship, he would throw them “into the furnace of fire” (Daniel 3:6). Even now Nebuchadnezzar says the same things to us, the true Hebrews, those who cross over. But, so that we may know by experience the heavenly dew that quenches every fire from us and cools our ruling mind, let us imitate those holy men. Perhaps even now Haman wants you, the Mordecais, to bow down to him (Esther 3:2); but you, Israel, must say: “I will not set the glory of men above the glory of God.”

Let us overthrow Bel by the word of God and kill the dragon with Daniel, so that, when we come near the mouths of lions, we may be beyond suffering any harm from them, while only those who are to blame for our present contest are devoured by the lions that cannot swallow us. Let us hold fast to this: among the brave deeds of Job this too is spoken: “[If] I laid my hand upon my mouth and kissed it, then let this too be counted to me as the greatest lawlessness” (Job 31:27-28). And it is likely that they will order us to put our hand to our mouth and kiss it.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 33); the old English was misaligned and largely invented: it gave a passage on refusing to worship sun, moon, stars and the emperor's image, with Daniel saying 'I worship nothing but the Lord my God', none of which is in this chapter, and it quoted Job 31:26 ('seeing the sun shining') where Origen quotes only Job 31:27-28. This chapter's own text (Nebuchadnezzar now, the dew, Haman and the Mordecais, Bel and the dragon, the lions, kissing the hand) is now translated in full.

Origen's quotation drops the conditional of Job 31:27 LXX (εἰ δὲ καὶ χεῖρά μου ἐπιθείς ...); the bracketed supplement [If] restores the sense of the oath of innocence, since the optative λογισθείη ('let it be counted') requires it.
'the true Hebrews, those who cross over': Origen's etymology of 'Hebrew' as 'one who crosses over' (περάτης).

choices.issue: OCR Auav, 4ανιήλ, Aoyısdein, εἰκὸς δὲ ὅτε, ἡμῶν τὴν χεῖρα
choices.choice: Read Ἀμάν, Δανιήλ, λογισθείη, ὅτι; ἡμῶν/ἡμῖν makes no difference to the sense ('order us to put our hand').
Ἀνανίας, Ἀζαρίας, Μισαήλ given in their familiar English forms, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael.

Koetschau closes the quotation before Ἰσραήλ, and the Septuagint of Mordecai's prayer (Esther 4:17e) ends at θεοῦ; so Ἰσραήλ is Origen's vocative: 'but you, Israel, must say'. Parent review checked the print and kept this reading.
